newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - November 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - November 8.

text.p: Following are the highlights of stories reported in the Irish press on Friday.

- The competition directorate in Brussels is to recommend to the European Commission next week that Telecom Eireann be allowed to keep its monopoly on voice telephony until 2000, instead of 1998 like most other EU states.

- The Irish Prime Minister, the Attorney General and the Minister for Justice are embroiled in potentially the most damaging controversy of their term in office so far as an inquiry begins into the circumstances leading to the sudden release and rearrest of 16 high-security prisoners.
- EU audits criticise Irish firms' grants.
- Slower September credit growth data eases interest rate fears.
- Government faces pay battle with nurses and teachers who seem likely to reject pay restructuring deals worth more than 120 million punts.
- Soccer whizkid Jason McAteer made a brief court appearance yesterday in an effort to secure an Irish passport in time for Sunday's World Cup qualifier against Iceland.
- Mackie shares dip 31 pence on the back of new profit warning.
- Jones Group Plc sells ship for 2.0 million punts.
